newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GarAgent sees higher op profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: GarAgent sees higher op profit in 1997.

text.p: Hungarian garage services company GarAgent Rt plans to post higher earnings in 1997 than in 1996 on which it will not pay dividend after shareholders' approval on Thursday, a company official said.

"In 1997 we plan one billion forints of sales revenues and a modest operating profit of 60 million forints and a financial loss of 20 million," Kalman Thaisz, GarAgent's president and CEO, told Reuters after the general meeting.
In 1996 GarAgent posted an operating profit of 37.4 million forints and a financial loss of 9.5 million on net sales of 864.7 forints. Last year it posted an after-tax profit of 23 million.
Thaisz said a more optimistic outlook was based on January-March figures and orders.
"Actual first quarter results and orders (for the first half of the year) show that 1997 will be much better than 1996," Thaisz said.
GarAgent is almost 30 percent owned by holding company Novotrade Rt which bought the stake through one of its subsidiaries earlier this month.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange GarAgent closed at 1,700 forints on April 21.
